q: What is the CBAM default value for urea and ammonia from India?
title: CBAM default value: Indian urea, ammonia
short: Indian solid urea under CN 3102 10 19 carries 2.220 t CO2e per tonne and anhydrous ammonia 3.280, both including indirect emissions. Fertilisers get a lower mark-up than other sectors: 1% from 2026, against 10% for steel in 2026.
audience: Indian urea, ammonia and nitrogen fertiliser producers and traders selling to the EU

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne (direct + indirect = total)

p: The default value mark-up for fertilisers is 1% from 2026 onwards, much lower than the 10% to 30% for other sectors, according to the Commission's guidance.

Defaults are set so they do not understate emissions, and the mark-up adds more. A plant with good fuel and production records will usually come in lower, and only a verified actual figure lets the importer use it.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.

sources.label: European Commission, Default values definitive period (Excel, version 2 of 6 August 2026), India sheet; legally binding values in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 correcting (EU) 2025/2621
European Commission, Guidance No. 3, CBAM methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods (14 August 2026), section 4.10
